verses.summary: Interest-taking and unjust appropriation; earlier Israelite interest restrictions are a legal comparison, not identical scope.
Those firmly grounded in knowledge affirm revelation and practice prayer and almsgiving; general religious motif.

God speaks to Moses and messengers known and unnamed; compare Moses' call narratives and distinguish direct divine speech from ordinary prophetic inspiration.
Messengers as bearers of good news and warnings, removing grounds for objection; widespread prophetic mission motif.
God and angels as witnesses to revelation; no source-specific account established on first pass.
Unbelief and obstructing God's path; general warning without established earlier discrete narrative.
Unbelief joined to injustice and exclusion from forgiveness; theological comparison needs exact scope.
Eternal punishment in Gehenna; compare later Jewish and Christian judgment language without equating their afterlife models.
Universal call to accept the messenger and divine ownership of heaven and earth; broad proclamation motif.
